title: Anglo-Peabody mine tussle leaves Indonesian mining firm seeking new coal assets
body: PT Buma Internasional is still on the hunt for coal assets, as uncertainty lingers about its planned purchase of a stake in the Dawson project.

title: South32 sees limited risk of Indonesia replicating nickel success in alumina
body: South32 reported a 75% surge in full-year profit on Thursday, helped by strong performance at its alumina division and higher commodity prices.

title: Freeport Indonesia to wrap up Gresik plant repairs by early September
body: Freeport expects to complete early next month repair work at its JV smelter in East Java.

title: Indonesia scraps coal pricing rules after pushback from buyers
body: Miners will now be allowed to sell below government-set benchmarks.

title: Freeport Indonesia to ramp up concentrate exports ahead of ban
body: The firm has exported about 65% of the quota as of mid-August.

title: Indonesia president signals intention to go after illegal mines
body: Indonesia will move to “rectify” illegal mines estimated to have caused $19 billion in state losses.

title: Nickel surpasses coal as Indonesia’s top export, Macquarie says
body: Earnings from overseas sales of nickel products were $16.5 billion in the first half of the year.

title: Indonesia discussing strategic management of critical minerals trade
body: Indonesia is one of only a only a handful of countries to strike a deal with Washington to lower US tariffs.

title: Indonesia Aims to Dominate Global Nickel and Electric Vehicle Battery Industries Through Strategic National Nickel Management
body: Indonesia has the potential to become a global hub for the nickel industry, with over 700 million tons of nickel reserves and 54 operational smelter facilities, as well as 49 others under construction. The country's nickel production is expected to fluctuate, with prices predicted to range from $15,000 to $16,000 next year, and the government is urged to address high production costs and regulatory challenges to maintain a competitive industry.

title: Indonesian Government Evaluates B40 Biodiesel Program Implementation with Mining Industry Stakeholders
body: The Indonesian government, through the Directorate General of New, Renewable, and Energy Conservation, held a discussion on the implementation of the 40% biodiesel program in the industrial sector, which has increased production costs in the nickel mining sector by 3-5%. The evaluation aims to find solutions to ensure the program's sustainability, considering factors such as global commodity prices and supply chain issues, particularly in regions like Sulawesi and Maluku.

title: Asosiasi Penambang Nikel Indonesia Evaluates B40 Implementation Amidst Industry Challenges
body: The Asosiasi Penambang Nikel Indonesia (APNI) has evaluated the implementation of B40, a program that has been in effect since January 2025, and reported a 3-5% increase in production costs in the nickel mining sector. The APNI also noted delays in supply chains in several regions, including Sulawesi Tenggara, Sulawesi Tengah, and Maluku Utara, which have impacted production operations.

title: Asosiasi Penambang Nikel Indonesia Releases Nickel Price Reference for September 2025, Showing a Decrease from the Previous Period
body: The Indonesian Nickel Miners Association (APNI) has announced the Nickel Price Reference (HMA) for September 2025, with a price of US$ 14.899,64 per dry metric ton, a decrease from the previous period's US$ 15.012,67 per dmt. The association also provided detailed pricing for nickel ore with varying moisture content and nickel grades, ranging from US$ 28,37 to US$ 43,80 per wet metric ton.

title: Global Nickel Prices Remain Stable, with Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate Experiencing a Significant Increase
body: The Indonesia Nickel Price Index reported stable global nickel prices, with the exception of Mixed Hydroxide Precipitate (MHP) which saw a significant increase of $97 per metric ton to $12,883 per metric ton. The stability in nickel prices reflects a balance between global supply and demand, while the surge in MHP prices is driven by the growing need for nickel-based battery materials in the Asian electric vehicle industry.

title: Indonesia's Nickel Industry Faces Trilemma in Implementing Environmental, Social, and Governance Standards
body: Indonesia's nickel industry is expected to face a trilemma of global demand, community price, and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) standards, with companies like PT Vale Indonesia and Ceria Corp already implementing ESG standards and remaining profitable. The industry aims to achieve a win-win situation by implementing ESG standards, with a focus on reducing carbon emissions, such as Vale's 28.7 ton CO2 per ton of nickel, and developing a green nickel market.

title: PT Bukit Asam Strengthens Local Economic Empowerment Through Desa Impian Program With Local Heroes Approach
body: PT Bukit Asam's Desa Impian program has successfully empowered local economies, with 80 beneficiaries and a collective annual revenue of Rp3.05 billion, and has also reduced illegal mining practices by transforming non-productive land into integrated agricultural centers. The program has also achieved significant environmental benefits, including the use of 12.5 tons of recycled conveyor belt waste and a reduction of 2.28 tons of CO₂ emissions per year through the use of solar-powered irrigation systems.

title: Menteri Lingkungan Hidup Apresiasi PT Vale Indonesia sebagai Contoh Investasi Lingkungan yang Progresif dan Berkelanjutan
body: PT Vale Indonesia Tbk telah mereklamasi lahan seluas 3.800 hektare di Sulawesi dan mengoperasikan tiga Pembangkit Listrik Tenaga Air dengan total kapasitas 365 MW, serta berhasil memanfaatkan kembali 100 persen limbah non-B3 pada 2024. Menteri Lingkungan Hidup Hanif Faisol Nurofiq menempatkan Vale Indonesia sebagai contoh nyata investasi lingkungan yang progresif dan berkelanjutan, dan berharap MIND ID dapat menjadi pemimpin dan penentu standar bagi industri pertambangan nasional.

title: Badan Pengelola Migas Aceh Proposes New Initiatives for 2026 to Boost National Oil and Gas Development and Support Energy Transition
body: The Badan Pengelola Migas Aceh (BPMA) has proposed new initiatives for 2026, including allocating Rp3.9 billion for exploration development in the North Sumatra Basin and Sibolga Basin, and Rp4.5 billion for monitoring and evaluating Carbon Capture Storage (CCS) and Carbon Capture Utilization and Storage (CCUS) in Aceh. These initiatives aim to accelerate national oil and gas development, support the energy transition agenda, and reduce carbon emissions in line with Indonesia's net zero emission target by 2060.
